description: The Landsat Ground Network page describes the five satellite ground stations that send commands to Landsat 8 and 9 and receive their telemetry and science data, and routes them into the Landsat ground system with the Data Collection and Routing System. The USGS Earth Resources Observation and Science Center in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, runs the primary station and coordinates the network; the others are Geoscience Australia's station at Alice Springs, a partner since 1979, NOAA's Fairbanks Command and Data Acquisition Station at Gilmore Creek, Alaska, a partner since 1982, the German Aerospace Center's station at Neustrelitz, a partner since 1999, and Kongsberg Satellite Services on Svalbard. A map shows each station's approximate contact area. History notes include hail destroying the first EROS antenna, after which a radome-covered replacement was installed in 1999. Coverage is global contact areas from five sites. Format and access: a free public web page. Licence: US federal public domain. Caveats: it gives station roles and history, not capacity or outage records. It documents a small, critical ground segment for resilience and capacity planning of Earth observation services. A related catalogue record is the NASA small spacecraft ground data systems chapter.
